solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Street act banned from getting louder ending in riot

indicators.note: being banned from something means being kept out of it, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: crescendo is the musical term for a passage that grows louder
to act is to do, so the word do stands for it

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken

explanation.surface: A street performance is stopped as the noise swells towards the close of a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banned from' removes DO from CRESCENDO, leaving CRESCEN, and 'ending in' takes the T at the end of riot.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescent is a curved row of houses and a common British street name, as in Royal Crescent in Bath.

clue.text: Switzerland's right out of the game, mate

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so the letter for right leaves the game

parts.note: rummy is a card game

explanation.surface: A Swiss player is told he can no longer play the game, pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes R from RUMMY, leaving UMMY.
explanation.definitionFit: Chummy is used as a noun of address, a friendly form like pal, for a fellow.

clue.text: Former European politician stops rent suddenly

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so these letters fill the middle of the other word

parts.note: rent as a past tense means tore
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A former EU politician suddenly prevents a rent payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid for housing but is the past tense of rend. 'stops' means plugs a gap, so the European politician sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore means without preparation, off the cuff, so done suddenly and on the spur of the moment.

clue.text: In America perhaps Green Party receives a suspension in one of its cities

indicators.note: receives means takes in, so the letter goes between the two pieces

parts.note: green is a colour, spelt the American way without the u
a do is a party
springs are part of a vehicle's suspension

explanation.surface: In the US, an environmental party is given a suspension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green Party' looks like the political party but splits in two, with 'receives' taking the A between them. 'In America perhaps' signals the US spelling, and 'its' refers back to America.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado Springs is a city in the US state of Colorado.

clue.text: Dig up source of embarrassment reflecting on leading candidate

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the reflected word comes first
reflecting means mirrored, so the letters of on are read backwards

parts.note: to mine is to dig up ore from the ground

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Unearthing something embarrassing reflects badly on the front-runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading candidate' reads as front-runner, but 'leading' puts the reflected word first; 'reflecting' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone put forward as a candidate for a post or award.

clue.text: Beach bum rants then departs

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means of poor quality, so the letters are knocked into a different order

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for departs, as on railway timetables

explanation.surface: A layabout on the beach complains loudly and then walks off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like a noun for the idler on the beach but works as an adjective meaning bad, turning RANTS into STRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Strand is an old and poetic word for a shore or beach, still seen in place names.

clue.text: RSC nuts audition cast for play

indicators.note: cast means thrown about or shaped anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Royal Shakespeare Company enthusiasts try out for parts in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The RSC is the Royal Shakespeare Company; 'cast' looks like giving actors parts but rearranges all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Andronicus is an early revenge tragedy by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Stay away from deserted area to start with

indicators.note: to start with means placed at the front of the other word

parts.note: void means empty or deserted

explanation.surface: Keep clear of the abandoned zone from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to keep away from or shun it.

clue.text: Underworld boss goes to prisons with Ecstasy to distribute

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
pens are enclosures for keeping animals or prisoners
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A crime lord is jailed with a drug he planned to sell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' looks like a gangster but is Dis, the Roman ruler of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense is to deal out or distribute, as a pharmacist dispenses medicine.

clue.text: Not just a place for amusement when not fine

indicators.note: when not tells us to drop the fine letter

parts.note: a funfair is a fairground with rides and stalls
f is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A funfair that won't impose penalties is somehow unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not just' reads as 'not only', but it is the definition meaning unjust.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair means unjust or not equitable.

clue.text: Up to no good in Winchester — on trial, oddly?

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letter for good is dropped from the weapon

parts.note: a Winchester is a famous make of rifle, so it stands for gun

indicators.note: oddly says to keep the letters in the odd positions of the word

explanation.surface: Someone causing mischief in the city of Winchester is now facing a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester is a cathedral city with a famous public school, but here it is the rifle. 'no' takes G from GUN, leaving UN; 'oddly' keeps T, I, L from trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Until and up to are interchangeable prepositions of time, as in open until or up to six o'clock.

clue.text: Note, sort involved in sumo wrestling will be huge

indicators.note: in places the note and the jumbled sort inside the other scrambled word
wrestling suggests bodies twisted about, so the letters of the word sumo are rearranged
involved means tangled or complicated, so the letters of sort are mixed up

explanation.surface: Anything you put into a sumo bout is bound to be enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrestling' turns sumo into MOUS and 'involved' turns sort into STRO; 'in' splits the first jumble around the note and the second. The image of sumo wrestlers makes the answer apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Monstrous can mean enormous, as something of monster size; the definition reads with 'will be' as the predicate link.

clue.text: Possessing zero money, Emma forged notes

indicators.note: possessing means holding within, so the anagram wraps round the other pieces
forged means fashioned or faked, so the letters of Emma are reworked

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A penniless woman called Emma has been faking banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' turns EMMA into MEMA, which holds O and RAND to give MEM-ORAND-A.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda are written notes or reminders; the word is the Latin plural of memorandum.

clue.text: This plant's the last to appear in herbaceous border

indicators.note: the last letter to appear in a word is its final one

parts.note: an edge is a border or margin

explanation.surface: A gardener observes that this plant is the final one to flower in the herbaceous border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'herbaceous border' reads as one gardening phrase, but it splits: the last letter of herbaceous, then border as EDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant of wet ground, so 'this plant' points to a particular species.

clue.text: In swindle, one goes for old act that's easy to carry off

definitions.text: act that's easy to carry off

indicators.note: one goes for old means the letter for one is replaced by the letter for old

parts.note: diddle is a British informal word meaning to swindle
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: In a con, a veteran performer takes on a routine that is simple to pull off.
explanation.walkthrough: DIDDLE is British slang for cheat. 'goes for' swaps its I for O.
explanation.definitionFit: A doddle is British slang for a task that is very easy to accomplish.

clue.text: They look after the Forest football team

definitions.meaning: forest wardens who guard woodland and its wildlife
a club name in football, most famously the Glasgow side

explanation.walkthrough: Nottingham Forest is an English football club, so 'the Forest football team' seems one phrase; it splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers are wardens who patrol woodland, and Rangers is also the name of several football clubs.

clue.text: Prom programme's framed by key composition of Adès

indicators.note: framed by means enclosed, so the programme sits within the key and the reworked name

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: a composition puts things together in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a plan is a programme or scheme

explanation.surface: A concert programme includes a piece in a certain key by the composer Thomas Adès.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prom' suggests the BBC Proms concerts, matching the musical surface, but it is short for promenade. 'composition of' turns the composer's name into SADE, and 'framed by' splits key plus SADE around the programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A prom is a seaside promenade, a paved walkway along the shore.

clue.text: What dealer may do with kitchen utensil

definitions.meaning: a drug dealer might keep a supply of cannabis in hand
a large pan for making soup or broth

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer's two halves separately: to stock is to keep a supply, and pot is slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpot is a deep pan in which stock or soup is simmered.

clue.text: Start to tackle cause of crime

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that one is used

parts.note: a reason is a cause or ground for something

explanation.surface: A detective sets out to address what motivates criminal behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country or sovereign.

clue.text: Resort's temperature is extremely pleasant

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera, and the s stays as a letter

explanation.surface: The weather at a holiday resort is very agreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicest is the superlative of nice, meaning most pleasant.

clue.text: Fool hides credit note, creating embarassing situation

indicators.note: hides means keeps something inside, so the fool's word wraps round the abbreviation

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool
cr is the accounting abbreviation for credit
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A foolish person conceals a bank credit slip and lands in an awkward predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' looks like a verb meaning trick but is the noun for a dupe; 'hides' wraps it round the credit abbreviation, and 'note' is a letter of the musical scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament one has got into, as in getting into scrapes.

clue.text: Consult an astrologer? Partly necessary for ruler's wife

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A ruler's wife might need to consult an astrologer.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'necessary for ruler's wife' as the definition, but 'necessary for' is a link: the answer means the ruler's wife alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is the wife of a sultan, a Muslim sovereign.

clue.text: Be unable to stand trial following case for defence?

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the trial goes after the case
the case of a word is its outside letters, first and last

parts.note: a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Someone in court cannot face the trial that follows the defence's case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case for defence' reads as a legal argument, but 'case' takes the outside letters D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe, unable to stand someone.

clue.text: Shrink's beginning to counsel one who's not settled?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: someone who has not settled a bill still owes, so is an ower

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist starts advising someone who cannot settle down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' looks like the noun for a psychiatrist, matching 'counsel', but it is the verb meaning flinch. OWER is a made-up word for a debtor, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to shrink back or cringe in fear.

clue.text: General election primarily needed after current uprising

indicators.note: needed after means placed behind, so the election letter follows
uprising in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a flow is a current

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A general election is called in the wake of a popular revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General election' looks like a single phrase, but 'General' is the definition: James Wolfe, the British general who took Quebec in 1759.
explanation.definitionFit: James Wolfe was a British army general famous for the capture of Quebec.

clue.text: Collection of columns Conan Doyle knocked out, having year off

indicators.note: knocked out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
having a letter off means it is removed
having a letter off means it is removed

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes's creator is beaten in a fight after taking a year's break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having ... off' removes Y from CONAN DOYLE, leaving CONANDOLE, and 'knocked out' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonnade is a row of columns supporting a roof or entablature.

clue.text: Europeans touring US city returned by way of not very large group of islands

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the Europeans wrap round the city

parts.note: Poles are natives of Poland, a European country

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters of the city are read in reverse

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the very letter

parts.note: via means by way of

explanation.surface: Travellers from Europe visit New York and come back through a vast cluster of Pacific islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' sends the city back to front and 'touring' wraps the Europeans round it; 'not' drops the very letter from the route word. 'large' belongs to the definition, since Polynesia is a vast Pacific region.
explanation.definitionFit: Polynesia is a vast region of the central Pacific made up of many island groups.

clue.text: Clapped-out vehicle achieves speed beyond 100

indicators.note: beyond means coming after, so speed follows the hundred

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
rate means speed, as in rate of knots

explanation.surface: An old banger somehow reaches more than a hundred miles an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is slang for an old, rickety car or aircraft.

clue.text: Empty tedium around hospital regularly defies belief

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the emptied word goes round the other pieces
an empty word has its contents removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: Sheer boredom on a hospital ward repeatedly seems beyond belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defies belief' reads as one idiom, but 'defies' is fodder; 'regularly' takes E, I, S. 'Empty' leaves T...M from tedium, round H and EIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in the existence of a god or gods.

clue.text: Form teacher's quietly seething, about to be dismissed

indicators.note: seething means churning, so the letters are stirred into a new order
dismissed means sent away, so this letter is taken out

parts.note: the letters of teacher's are used whole, including the s
c is short for circa, Latin for about
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A form teacher is quietly furious about being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form teacher' reads as a schoolteacher, but 'Form' is the definition. 'to be dismissed' removes C from TEACHERS, and 'seething' rearranges TEAHERS plus P.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap sheet is an official form or record listing a person's criminal convictions.
